mission_goal: self.root / human-surface Frank v0.1 fully operational on accepted Hostinger Ubuntu VPS

zero_cost_evidence.claim: NVIDIA documents hosted NIM chat completions at integrate.api.nvidia.com with POST /v1/chat/completions; zero-cost eligibility remains separately fail-closed by runtime policy.
zero_cost_evidence.counterhypothesis: A configured credential can belong to a different billing or production context; request execution must stay on the documented provider operation and remain blocked by zero-cost policy when entitlement is not established.

invariants: Never serialize, log, commit, echo or display API secret values.
Never access Together, including discovery, probes, routing and fallback.
Never make a paid request unless the project owner separately authorizes a nonzero budget.
A configured key is capability evidence, not proof of quota, billing state or health.
Except for an officially documented zero-cost developer entitlement or explicit host-side zero-cost attestation, a configured key is not eligible for routing.
A provider credential may only be sent to that provider's exact typed remote endpoint capability; a global multi-provider host allowlist is forbidden.

Credential binding compares scheme, host, effective port and exact canonical provider base path; remote query, fragment, params, dot-segment aliases and percent-encoded path aliases are rejected before request construction.
Provider endpoint URLs containing userinfo are rejected before request construction or network access.
Authenticated provider requests must not follow HTTP redirects; redirects fail closed before credentials can cross an origin boundary.
The text-chat adapter validates a nonempty model plus object messages with nonempty string roles and string content before network access; typed multimodal requests require a separate adapter.

Execution receipt request IDs bind provider, a digest of the complete request target and the serialized request digest and remain stable across exact retries; attempt IDs are unique per execution attempt.
Attempt IDs include a fresh high-entropy nonce so equal-time concurrent attempts cannot alias; raw nonces are never serialized.
A response reaches VERIFIED only when choices is a non-empty list whose first message is an object with string content; malformed JSON shapes fail closed with a receipt.
An HTTP status response, including 402, 429 and 5xx, proves EXECUTED transport but never VERIFIED or DONE; connection and timeout failures without an HTTP response remain unexecuted.
Every received non-2xx status remains unverified even when the transport returns it as a regular response object instead of raising HTTPError.
Malformed bodies preserve the received HTTP status and classify as invalid_provider_response; connection or timeout failures without a response use null status and unreachable_provider.
Once response headers and status are received, body-read failures preserve that status and EXECUTED while classifying as incomplete_provider_response; they never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Every real provider request must emit a redacted execution receipt.
Rate limits and provider faults trigger bounded cooldown and rerouting, never retry storms.
HTTP 402 remains a fail-closed unresolved payment-authority signal until a durable same-budget-epoch payment latch is implemented and independently validated.
